newsitem.title: USA: Versace had no regrets, but wanted to "live forever". [CORRECTED 22:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Versace had no regrets, but wanted to "live forever". [CORRECTED 22:47 GMT]

text.p: After a bout with cancer last year, Gianni Versace said in a series of interviews that while he had no regrets about his life, he wanted to live forever, The New Yorker magazine reported.

"When, after the analyses, counter-analyses, CAT-scans, and so on, I realised that it was possible that at not even 50 years old I could just ... go, I said to myself, 'Well, every day that I live from now on -- it's my party,'" the magazine reported in its July 28 issue.
"I thought, Benissimo. If I have to die, I can thank God that I have lived 49 fantastic years. I don't have any regrets; I've always done what I wanted," the magazine quoted Versace as saying.

It said Versace, who was murdered last week at the age of 50 in Miami Beach, Florida, had been diagnosed with a rare cancer in 1996 (corrects the year from 1986), but that the cancer was successfully treated.
"I have a splendid family, a tranquil personal life. I adore the work I do," Versace, a renown fashion designer, was quoted as saying.
Asked what he would change about his life, Versace, replied: "It would be the passing of time. I'd like to live forever. If there's anything I'm afraid of it's missing what will happen tomorrow ...."

"I want to see my nieces and nephews grow up -- see their children. I won't miss being young, because we all know we'll be old in 20 or 30 years. But one day I'll miss the people I love. I get crazy at the idea that a time will come when I won't see Daniel and Allegra anymore," he said of the children of his sister Donatella.
